summary: One product in a shop's listing, carrying what a buyer chooses by.
not_for: A comparison of a few products side by side: collection.table.index.

slots.when: What the shop attaches to the offer, tagged [offer]: shipping (送料無料 or the fee), points, the delivery date, the seller.
The average and the number of ratings, as two values.
The stock state where it limits the purchase: 在庫切れ, 残り2点.

rules.rule: The rating shows the average and the number of ratings.
One to three attributes specific to the category (capacity, size).
The attribute the buyer sorted or filtered by is shown.
Every attribute shown can be filtered by.
The price is the strongest text of the item: larger and heavier than the title, which runs two or three lines and then truncates.
On a Japanese shop the shipping (送料無料 or the fee) sits beside the price, and the points, the rating with its count, the delivery date and the seller follow where the shop has them.

evidence.says: Product list items need the image, the title, the price, the rating with its count, the variations, and one to three category-specific attributes.

evidence.source: Baymard Institute, Contextual list item information (2015)
evidence.says: List items should show the attribute the user sorted or filtered on.

evidence.source: Baymard Institute, Filters for list item information (2019)
evidence.says: 38% of sites show list item information the user cannot filter by.

evidence.source: Search-result pages of Amazon.co.jp, 楽天市場, Yahoo!ショッピング, メルカリ, アスクル and 価格.com, captured 2026-11 (research/20261113-production-ui-ooui/corpus/anatomy_shop_results.json)
evidence.says: The price is 20 to 24px and bold against a 14 to 16px regular title on 6 of 7 pages, and red on 6 of 7; shipping wording on 5 of 7, points on 4 of 7, a rating with its count on 5 of 7, the seller on 5 of 7; tax wording on 1 of 7.
